title: api-gateway: tune streaming proxy buffers, routing rules, and OpenAI-compat streaming semantics
author: Avery Malik
release_notes: Adjusts default streaming proxy buffer sizes and routing behavior for large payloads; improves OpenAI-compat streaming (function/tool-calls) to reduce dropped chunks under backpressure. No API surface contract changes expected for customers, but behavior for extremely large streaming payloads may change.
description:
Motivation: Production incidence during high-concurrency streaming (SUP-814) showed repeated small drops and reordering of streaming chunks when requests hit routing paths with payload-size-based fallbacks. This manifested as partial function/tool-calls being delivered to downstream integrations and intermittent structured-output truncation. Root causes: conservative proxy buffer defaults, routing rule order that prioritized cost-tier over payload-compatibility, and subtle mismatch in how we translated OpenAI-chunked semantic events to our internal stream frames.

This PR makes three coordinated changes to improve stability and reduce customer-visible errors: 1) Increase and make proxy streaming buffer sizes adaptive to request-size and model-tier to avoid mid-stream flushes; 2) Reorder routing rules and add an explicit payload-size compatibility check so openai-compat streaming routes (function/tool-call flows and structured-output) are routed to nodes with buffer profiles that will preserve chunk boundaries; 3) Harden OpenAI-compat stream event translation to ensure function_call and tool invocation events are not split across frames and add a small reassembly window for reordering/late chunks.

What changed (high-level):
- api-gateway/proxy/streaming_buffer.go: introduce adaptive buffer profile selection and a default increase for high-concurrency hosts. Buffer selection is influenced by request Content-Length and model profile metadata.
- api-gateway/routing/rules.go: add PayloadSizeCompatible(rule, request) predicate and reorder rules so that openai-compat streaming routes evaluate payload compatibility before lower-cost fallbacks.
- api-gateway/handlers/openai_compat.go: make streaming event serializer preserve semantic boundaries for function_call and tool invocation events; add small reassembly buffer and sequence checks.
- api-gateway/config/defaults.go: expose two new feature flags and defaults: StreamingProxy.AdaptiveBuffers=true, StreamingProxy.DefaultBufferBytes=16384 (previously 4096), StreamingProxy.MaxReassemblyWindowMs=250.
- tests/unit/streaming_proxy_test.go: add tests that simulate partial chunk delivery, reordering, and validate reassembly and boundary preservation.
- docs/api-gateway/streaming.md: document behavior changes, tuning knobs, and rollback steps.

Checklist: [x] Unit tests added/updated [x] Integration test scenario for SUP-814 added [x] Performance sanity checked locally with stress harness [ ] Add e2e load test to perf-canary (follow-up)

Compatibility and customer impact: There is no change to public REST API or wire formats. Customers that have tuned or relied on very small streaming buffer behavior may notice fewer split events (which is desirable). Operators can opt out by setting StreamingProxy.AdaptiveBuffers=false.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind config flag (defaults enabled). Will deploy to canary (us-west-2) first, monitor streaming chunk drop rate, and then roll to global. Metrics to watch: streaming.chunk_drops, streaming.reassembly_failures, api.gateway.latency.p50/p95.

Testing performed: unit tests (added), integration test against a local mininet with delayed chunks, canary run under synthetic load showing 88% reduction in chunk_drops for SUP-814 scenario. CI: initial lint and unit run failed due to a race in streaming_buffer.go; race fixed and tests re-run.

Related: SUP-814 (incident), ENG-1934 (routing policy work), ENG-1978 (openai-compat streaming stability).
commits: feat(api-gateway): add adaptive streaming proxy buffer profiles and selection
fix(proxy): avoid flush-on-full during large-chunk streaming by using backpressure-aware write
chore(config): expose streaming proxy defaults and reassembly window flags
feat(routing): add PayloadSizeCompatible predicate and reorder openai-compat routes
fix(openai-compat): preserve function_call/tool invocation boundaries in stream serializer
test(streaming): add unit tests for reassembly and out-of-order chunk handling
docs: update api-gateway streaming docs with tuning guide
files_changed: api-gateway/proxy/streaming_buffer.go -- implements adaptive buffer profiles and backpressure-aware write path (see SelectBufferProfile(request) and writeWithBackpressure)
api-gateway/routing/rules.go -- add PayloadSizeCompatible predicate and reorder rule evaluation for openai-compat routes
api-gateway/handlers/openai_compat.go -- serializer changes to keep function_call / tool events intact, reassembly buffer logic and sequence checks
api-gateway/config/defaults.go -- new feature flags StreamingProxy.AdaptiveBuffers, StreamingProxy.DefaultBufferBytes, StreamingProxy.MaxReassemblyWindowMs
tests/unit/streaming_proxy_test.go -- new unit tests exercising partial-chunk delivery and reassembly
docs/api-gateway/streaming.md -- doc updates and tuning guidance
diff_snippets:
--- a/api-gateway/config/defaults.go
+++ b/api-gateway/config/defaults.go
@@
-    StreamingProxy.DefaultBufferBytes = 4096
+    StreamingProxy.DefaultBufferBytes = 16384 // increased to reduce mid-stream flushes for large chunks
+    StreamingProxy.AdaptiveBuffers = true
+    StreamingProxy.MaxReassemblyWindowMs = 250

--- a/api-gateway/handlers/openai_compat.go
+++ b/api-gateway/handlers/openai_compat.go
@@
-    // old: naive chunk write
-    writer.Write(chunk)
+    // new: ensure semantic boundaries preserved; use reassembly buffer when sequence gaps seen
+    if chunk.BeginsSemanticBoundary() {
+        flushReassemblyBuffer()
+        writer.Write(chunk)
+    } else {
+        reassemblyBuffer.Append(chunk)
+    }
reviews: Samir Patel (reviewer): Overall solid. Two concerns: 1) Default increase to 16KB seems large for high fanout; did you measure memory/FD impact? 2) Routing reorder could change cost characteristics for some tenants. Please add safety tests and a config flag to revert.\nAuthor (Avery): Measured memory impact in canary: ~1.2% heap increase for proxy worker under 5000 concurrency; added adaptive profile (small/medium/large) so we only apply 16KB for large payloads. Added StreamingProxy.AdaptiveBuffers flag per request.

Leah Ortiz (reviewer): Nice tests. Please add an integration scenario where function_call events are deliberately split across 3 chunks and one is delayed by 120ms to validate reassembly window. Also add a small explanatory comment in routing rules about why payload compatibility must be checked earlier.\nAuthor (Avery): Added the integration scenario and the comment. Reassembly window default tuned to 250ms after test iterations.
Ravi Chandrasekhar (reviewer, approver): Verified local stress results and unit tests; approving pending CI green.\nMaintainer (Meredith Liu): Merging after CI pass and canary observation.
